Welcome.Title: MR- Bruja
Welcome.Body: An old witch, an heir to find, and a Director who puts the world in her way. Both of you sit down in the Hut. This unofficial system needs the book “Bruja”.

Safety.Intro: Pause, Veil or X-Card: they alert the whole table instantly, without saying who pressed it.
Safety.PauseText: The game stops for a moment.
Safety.VeilHint: Tell it without going into detail.
Safety.VeilText: We'll pass over this, without detail.
Safety.XHint: Not this. Skip it and don't ask.
Safety.XText: That stays out of the story. We take another road.
Safety.Anonymous: Nobody will know who triggered it; the X-Card is not recorded anywhere.
Safety.Topics: Before starting, talk about lines and veils: witch persecution and burning, torture, violence against children or death can be hard topics.

Access.Title: Accessibility and reading
Access.Intro: Personal settings: they only affect this system's windows and only in your browser.
Access.darkModeHint: Everything dark: sheets, parchments, cards and notes. No bright backgrounds to dazzle.
Access.wideSpacingHint: More air between lines and letters.
Access.reducedMotionHint: No animations, smoke or moving flames.
Access.reducedEffectsHint: No moths, smoke or floating embers.
Access.musicHint: Very sparse harp at big moments.
Access.mesaVentanaHint: The Hut is a window you can move and resize, instead of filling the screen.

Diagnostic.Hint: A copyable report of the system's state, in case something fails.
Diagnostic.Problems: There are problems; copy the report and send it.

Rules.Disclaimer: A summary in my own words, to keep at hand. The book rules.
Rules.PrepText: The Witch needs a name, a trait and a bag with three objects: one to find her way, one to trade and one to eat.
Rules.ScenesText: The Witch picks the scene type and the pawn goes on it. She can't repeat the previous type (unless she rests). Frame who, where and what happens, and play as long as needed.
Rules.RollText: When there is conflict, roll 2d6, plus a third if the trait or an object comes into play (max 3d6). Rolling closes the scene.
Rules.ConsText: The Director writes them in secret. With five, the witch dies without an heir.
Rules.PdText: Successes give them. They are spent before rolling (the die) or outside a roll.

Cost.dado: One more die on the roll (max 3d6).
Cost.descanso: Rest: choose any scene type (even a repeat) and +1 die in that scene.
Cost.hada: A fairy or spirit visits: one consequence is removed.
Cost.marcar: Mark an NPC as a potential heir; another consequence is removed.
Cost.elegir: Choose a marked heir: an epilogue with no dice.

Rules.EndText: With five consequences the witch dies. With an heir chosen (at least 9 DP earned over the game), the game ends whenever you like.
Rules.SoloText: One person can take both seats. Two people can take turns as the Witch, leaving the Director to the other.
Rules.BookEmpty: You haven't imported your manual's text yet.
Rules.BookHow: The book's PDF is made of images, so it is read with OCR on your computer (it never leaves it). Run this in the system folder and press “Reload”:

empezar.Title: First steps
empezar.Description: How to set up the game: seats, witch and bag. About three minutes.

bienvenida.Title: A witch, an heir
bienvenida.Text: Welcome to Bruja. An old witch is leaving the world and needs someone to take over her hut. Two people play: the Witch and the Game Director, who plays everyone else. This system handles the dice, the candles and the grimoire; the game's rulebook is still essential. Move forward and back with the buttons below and leave whenever you like.

choza.Title: The Hut
choza.Text: This is the Hut, your table. It can be a window or fill the whole screen: the arrows button, top right, switches between them. The whole game state is here and both of you see it at once.

asientos.Title: The two seats
asientos.Text: Both of you sit down: one as the Witch and one as the Director. If you play solo, take both. Each person sees and does their own part: the Director's secret notebook only opens in their browser.

bruja.Title: Name and trait
bruja.Text: The Witch needs a name (maybe a nickname) and a trait: what defines her, her looks, her temper or what she can do. The italic buttons are ideas from the setting: press one to fill the field and change it as you like.

bolsa.Title: The bag with three objects
bolsa.Text: Her bag holds three objects: one to find her way, one to trade and one to eat. No compass, money or food: let your imagination run. Later these objects can help her on a roll.

ambientacion.Title: The setting
ambientacion.Text: Here is the setting: places, characters and dangers to inspire you. Follow it, ignore it or add your own with other modules.

empezar.Title: Out of the hut
empezar.Text: When you are both seated and the witch has a name, a trait and three objects, press Set out to find an heir. Under “Game options” you can start with drama points or turn on the “last breath”.

siguiente.Title: Now, let's play
siguiente.Text: Once the game starts, open the next tutorial, The table in play: it shows the cards, the cauldron, the candles and the drama points. You'll find it under Settings → Guided tutorial.

mesa.Title: The table in play
mesa.Description: Cards, cauldron, candles, drama points and heirs. About four minutes.

intro.Title: One scene after another
intro.Text: The game is about scenes: the Witch picks a type, you play as long as needed and, if there is conflict, you roll. Rolling closes the scene. Successes give drama points and failures give consequences. With five consequences the witch dies without an heir; if she gets an heir, she wins. (If you haven't started the game yet, some elements will appear later: this tour is still valid.)

cartas.Title: The five scene cards
cartas.Text: Action, Reaction, Drama, Monologue and Retrospection. The Witch picks one and the pawn goes on it. She can't repeat the previous type (it's greyed out) unless she rests (2 DP). The cards button, above, switches between engraved and neutral cards.

libro.Title: The scene is an open book
libro.Text: On the left you frame it: who is there? where? what is happening? In a few words, between the two of you. Narrate as needed; you only roll when there is conflict.

uso.Title: Trait or object in play
uso.Text: If the trait or a bag object helps, the Witch proposes it in a sentence and the Director decides whether to grant it. If granted, a third die is rolled.

caldero.Title: The cauldron
caldero.Text: The dice fall into the cauldron: 2d6 (3 with a trait, an object or a rest). The result shows its name and effect: drama points, consequences or both.

cierre.Title: Closing the scene
cierre.Text: Rolling closes the scene: write how it ends in a sentence or two, and everything goes into the Grimoire.

velas.Title: The five candles
velas.Text: Each consequence snuffs a candle. The Director writes them in secret: you only see how many are still lit.

frasco.Title: The drama points flask
frasco.Text: Drama points fill the flask. The bar below advances toward the 9 you need, over the whole game, to be able to win.

recetas.Title: The recipes
recetas.Text: Points buy the recipes: one more die, a fairy's visit, marking an heir (4) and choosing her (5), which leads to the epilogue with no dice.

herederas.Title: The heirs
herederas.Text: The heirs you mark appear here with their wax seal. Up to six fit; only one is chosen.

herramientas.Title: The tools
herramientas.Text: Left to right: full screen or window, hide the table (in full screen), engraved or neutral cards, the Director's notebook, the Grimoire (the story played), Rules, Safety (pause, veil and X-card) and Accessibility, with dark mode.

fin.Title: Good luck
fin.Text:
That's it. If you are the Director, the next tutorial shows your secret notebook.
Under Settings → Guided tutorial you can repeat any of them.

director.Title: The Director and the notebook
director.Description: Granting traits, writing consequences in secret and the notebook key. About three minutes.

intro.Title: The Game Director
intro.Text: You play everyone else —villagers, fairies, wolves— and keep what the Witch doesn't know: the consequences. This tour is for whoever holds the Director's seat.

conceder.Title: Granting the trait or object
conceder.Text: When the Witch proposes using her trait or an object, you decide here: Grant or Deny. Be as lax as you like; the game rewards imagination.

anotar.Title: Writing the consequence
anotar.Text: When a roll gives consequences this notice appears: write it in secret, with a sentence you can use later. The sparks give ideas, but never write for you. If the Witch spends points on a fairy or an heir, it will ask you here which consequence goes away.

boton.Title: Your notebook
boton.Text: This button opens your Director's Notebook, the yellow page. Only you see it: the Witch knows how many consequences she carries, not which.

lista.Title: The consequences
lista.Text: All of them are here, with their text. You can edit them, remove them when they get resolved in the story or reveal them: their text becomes public and goes into the Grimoire.

clave.Title: The notebook key
clave.Text: The notebook is stored encrypted: not even the console lets the Witch read it. The key lives only in this browser. Copy it with the key button and keep it: without it you can't open the notebook from another browser or computer.

candidatas.Title: Candidates and NPCs
candidatas.Text: Note your heir candidates and other NPCs here. Marking one costs the Witch 4 drama points; until then it's up to you.

fin.Title: That's all
fin.Text:
Remember: your secret notes never leave your notebook unless you reveal them.
Good luck with the witch.
